claims.statement: For every finite nonconstant Boolean source, a maximum-ratio physical descendant is critical. If a disjoint tensor product F of nonconstant Boolean factors is eta-critical under every physical descendant and w_j=I(f_j)/I(F), then R(F)-(1-w_j)eta/w_j <= R(f_j) <= R(F)+eta and every descendant u of f_j has R(u)<=R(f_j)+eta/w_j. Consequently an exact critical tensor product is precisely a product of equal-ratio critical factors. A one-point surgery of an arbitrary lifted core is nonfactorable across the old/new split while its H, I, and H/I converge to those of the core.
claims.quantifiers: All finite uniform Boolean cubes; every nonconstant Boolean source; all finite disjoint tensor factorizations; every eta>=0; all nonconstant physical coordinate restrictions.
hypotheses: Tensor blocks are disjoint physical coordinate blocks
Eta-criticality compares with every nonconstant physical descendant
scope_exclusions: No bounded ratio for prime critical sources
No claim that one-point surgery preserves criticality
No pruning of abstract connected support components
